## `scripts/ai/chatter_minds.gd`

class_name `ChatterMinds` · extends `Node`

The voices of the global chat and of face-to-face talk (slice C §3). Residents, and sometimes a mayor, talk about real city events in their own voices: one batched GMI call per ambient round, one per player chat message, one per spoken line in a conversation, all through GmiClient.live_json (never remember/lookup, so nothing reaches the session cache or a save). Offline a deterministic heuristic writes the lines from each resident's own say, thought, mood reason, job, skills, traits and home. Live answers live only in this node's in-memory LRU.

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `T = preload("res://scripts/fp/chat/chat_text.gd")`
- `MODEL_NAMES = ["deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash", "google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite", "Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash"]`: The fast models chatter rotates across, taken from ResidentMinds.MODELS.
- `ROUND_TOKENS = 600`
- `ROUND_TIMEOUT = 30.0`
- `TALK_TOKENS = 300`
- `TALK_TIMEOUT = 20.0`
- `MAX_LINES = 8`
- `LINE_CHARS = 140`
- `LRU_MAX = 256`
- `EMOTES = ["wave", "shrug", "angry", "laugh", "none"]`
- `MAYOR_LINE_CHANCE = 0.35`
- `ROUND_SYSTEM = """`
- `PLAYER_SYSTEM = """`
- `TALK_SYSTEM = """`
- `EVENT_NOUN = { "fire": "fire", "blackout": "blackout", "sewage_burst": "sewage leak", "gridlock": "g...`: Short noun for each disaster type, as residents say it.
- `COMPLAINT_LINES = { "power": ["Lights went out on my block again.", "No power at home since this morning....`
- `AMBIENT_LINES = { "morning": ["Coffee first, city later.", "Morning, {district}. Bus was on time for on...`
- `REACT = { "grump": ["And {mayor} is where, exactly?", "Of course it's {district}. It's always {...`
- `AGREE = { "grump": ["{afirst} gets it.", "Exactly what I said yesterday, {afirst}.", "Yep. Nobo...`
- `DISAGREE = { "grump": ["Not buying it, {afirst}.", "Easy for you to say, {afirst}.", "Come see {st...`
- `INCIDENT_REACT = { "grump": ["Another {ev}. Who's running this place?", "{afirst}, don't hold your breat...`: Replies to an incident, by voice ({ev}, {place}, {street}, {work}, {afirst}).
- `MAYOR_STYLE = [ "Crews are dispatched to {place}. Utilities first, then cleanup.", "Rerouting around ...`

### Properties

- `last_system: String`: The last prompts built (tests read them; never saved, logged or printed).
- `recent_of: Callable`: Optional: func(resident_id: String) -> Array[String], the resident's last chat lines (talk prompt).

### Functions

- `func setup(p_sim: CitySim, p_people: Residents, p_client: GmiClient, p_brain: CityBrain, p_directory: CityDirectory) -> void`: Wires the minds to the city. client may be offline (live_enabled false): then no call is made.
- `func busy(kind: String) -> bool`: True while a call of this kind ("round", "player" or "talk") is in flight.
- `func live() -> bool`: True when calls go to the network (offline gates: always false).
- `func reset() -> void`: Forgets per-city state (load, New City); the LRU and stats survive.
- `func run_round(topic: Dictionary, recent: Array) -> Array`: One batched round: 4-8 lines from 4-6 picked residents (and maybe a mayor) about a topic. Coroutine; returns validated lines [{"id", "author", "role", "district", "text", "reply_to", "reply_idx"}] (reply_to is a shown seq from recent, reply_idx an earlier line of this round).
- `func reply_to_player(text: String, district: int, recent: Array) -> Array`: Replies to a player chat line (2-4 residents, district-weighted). text may hold several coalesced lines joined by "\n". Coroutine; same line dicts as run_round (reply_to -1: the caller points them at the player's message).
- `func talk(r: Dictionary, turns: Array, player_text: String) -> Dictionary`: One face-to-face reply from resident r: {"reply", "mood_delta", "memory", "emote", "source"}. turns: earlier lines [{"who": "you"|"them", "text"}]. Coroutine: one live call when online (falls back to the LRU, then the heuristic), the heuristic offline.
- `func talk_user(r: Dictionary, turns: Array, said: String) -> String`: The talk prompt's user JSON: the resident's card with directory names instead of coordinates, state, plan, thought, mood reason, last 8 memories, what is nearby, their last 3 chat lines, the last 6 turns and player_line (the only place the player's text appears).
- `func validate_talk(data: Dictionary) -> Dictionary`: Validates a talk reply: reply <= 40 words (debranded, no URL, no model name), mood_delta in -1..1, memory <= 15 words, emote whitelisted. {} when the reply is unusable.
- `func greeting(r: Dictionary) -> String`: The first thing r says when the player walks up: their own "say" line, else a greeting in their voice.
- `func greeting_emote(r: Dictionary) -> String`: The emote that goes with r's greeting: a wave from friendly voices, a frown when miserable.
- `func talk_heuristic(r: Dictionary, turns: Array, said: String) -> Dictionary`: Deterministic offline reply in r's voice (C §4 "Offline"): answers the quick questions from the resident's real state and keywords in free text from their job, home and the city.
- `func pick_participants(topic: Dictionary, k: int, rng: RandomNumberGenerator, must: Array = []) -> Array[Dictionary]`: Picks k residents for topic, weighted by proximity to the topic tile (or the player's district), matching skills for incidents, sociable / outspoken traits (shy down) and extreme moods. must: resident ids that join first (named in a player line).
- `func chat_card(r: Dictionary) -> Dictionary`: The compact prompt card of a chat participant: id, name, job, traits, mood, mood reason, the last 2 memories, home and work as directory names (never coordinates).
- `func clean_card(c: Dictionary) -> Dictionary`: resident.card() with every coordinate replaced by directory names (talk prompts).
- `func topic_facts(topic: Dictionary) -> Dictionary`: Topic facts for prompts (names only, never coordinates).
- `func validate_lines(data: Dictionary, picked: Array, mayor: int, recent: Array) -> Array`: Validates model lines (C §3): ids must be picked (or "m<mayor>"), text trimmed to 140 and debranded; empty lines, URLs, model names and more than 2 sentences are dropped; at most 8.
- `func heuristic_round(topic: Dictionary, picked: Array, mayor: int, recent: Array, rng: RandomNumberGenerator) -> Array`: Deterministic offline round: an opener on the topic from the first participant, then reactions, agreements and disagreements in each participant's voice, threaded by reply_idx.
- `func heuristic_player(said: String, picked: Array, rng: RandomNumberGenerator) -> Array`: Deterministic offline replies to the player's line, by what the line is about.
- `static func intent_of(text: String) -> String`: Coarse intent of a player line: greet, how, around, mayor, bye, power, water, traffic, money, jobs, incident, crime, food, fun, news, who, help or generic.
- `static func voice(r: Dictionary) -> String`: A resident's voice: grump, worried, sunny, civic or plain (traits first, then mood).
- `func facts(r: Dictionary, topic: Dictionary = {}) -> Dictionary`: Template tokens for r: first, name, job, district, street, work, mayor, mayor_last, place, ev, ev_cap, what, headline, label, tax (and the topic's when given).
- `func lru_get(key: String) -> Variant`: The cached live answer for key, or null.
- `func lru_put(key: String, value: Variant) -> void`: Stores a live answer (never saved, never flushed, never written through GmiClient).
- `func lru_size() -> int`: Entries in the LRU.

## `scripts/ai/city_brain.gd`

class_name `CityBrain` · extends `Node`

Puts GMI model inference on every layer of the city. Each in-game day it batches: - 5 AI mayors (different models) that read their district map and issue build/zone/tax actions - Citizen Voices: sampled residents describe their lives; complaints feed back to mayors - GridFall Gazette: a news editor writes the day's headline from real events - Chaos Director: picks disasters that probe the city's weaknesses - Grid Operator: sets load-shedding priority when power or water runs short - Council Speaker: rules on ordinance proposals using the mayors' votes plus an on-demand Street Inspector that role-plays whatever tile the player clicks. Live calls fall back to the recorded replay cache, then to local heuristics.

### Signals

- `mayor_thinking(mi: int)`
- `mayor_decided(mi: int, decision: Dictionary)`
- `citizens_spoke(voices: Array)`
- `news_published(paper: Dictionary)`
- `council_ruled(ruling: Dictionary)`
- `chaos_decided(decision: Dictionary)`
- `operator_decided(decision: Dictionary)`
- `inspector_answered(report: Dictionary)`
- `busy_changed(pending: int)`

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `MAX_WAIT_MS = 75000`

### Functions

- `func setup(p_sim: CitySim, p_client: GmiClient) -> void`
- `func pending_calls() -> int`
- `func mayors_pending() -> int`
- `func send_decree(text: String) -> void`
- `func spread_pending() -> bool`: True while the day round still has pieces waiting for a frame (the sim's spread gate).
- `func day_of_sim() -> int`
- `func residents_spoke(_day: int) -> void`: With AI residents, the voices the mayors hear are the residents' own words from today's plans.
- `func inspect_tile(x: int, y: int) -> void`
- `func to_dict() -> Dictionary`
- `func from_dict(d: Dictionary) -> void`

## `scripts/ai/gmi_client.gd`

class_name `GmiClient` · extends `Node`

Async GMI Cloud chat client with JSON extraction, a recorded replay cache, and heuristic fallback. Every call is logged with its source (live / cache / heuristic).

### Signals

- `call_logged(record: Dictionary)`
- `breaker_changed(state: String)`: The circuit breaker moved to state ("closed" / "open" / "half_open").

### Constants

- `CHAT_URL = "https://api.gmi-serving.com/v1/chat/completions"`
- `MAX_RETRIES = 2`: Retries after the first attempt, for transient failures only (see is_retryable()).
- `BACKOFF_BASE_MS = 500`
- `BACKOFF_CAP_MS = 4000`
- `LIVE_WINDOW = 20`: Live outcomes kept for the failure-ratio alert.
- `RETRY_RESULTS = [HTTPRequest.RESULT_CANT_CONNECT, HTTPRequest.RESULT_CANT_RESOLVE, HTTPRequest.RESULT_C...`: Network results worth another attempt; TLS, redirect, body-size and file errors are not.
- `RETRY_HTTP = [408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504]`
- `REPLAY_CACHE_PATH = "res://data/gmi_replay_cache.json"`
- `SESSION_CACHE_PATH = "user://gmi_session_cache.json"`
- `MAX_LOG = 300`
- `MODEL_EXTRAS = { "deepseek-ai/": {"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}}, "moonshotai/": {"thinking": {"typ...`: Hybrid reasoning models spend the whole token budget thinking unless told not to. Keys are model-id prefixes; values are merged into the request body.

### Properties

- `breaker`: Opens after 4 consecutive service failures; while open, chat_json goes straight to the cache or heuristic and live_json fails fast with "circuit open".
- `live_outcomes: Array[bool]`: The last LIVE_WINDOW live outcomes (true = ok), oldest first.

### Functions

- `func has_key() -> bool`
- `func set_live(enabled: bool) -> void`
- `func breaker_state() -> String`: "closed", "open" or "half_open" (an open breaker past its cool-down reads half_open).
- `func live_failure_ratio() -> float`: Share of failed live calls among the last LIVE_WINDOW (0 when none).
- `static func is_retryable(result_code: int, http_code: int) -> bool`: True for failures another attempt may fix: transient network results, 408, 429 and 500/502/503/504.
- `static func is_service_failure(result_code: int, http_code: int) -> bool`: True when the failure says the service (not the request or the reply) is unhealthy; these count toward opening the breaker.
- `static func backoff_ms(attempt: int, jitter01: float) -> int`: Delay before retry number attempt (0-based): exponential from BACKOFF_BASE_MS, capped at BACKOFF_CAP_MS, with "equal jitter" (jitter01 in 0..1 picks a point in the upper half).
- `func chat_json(role: String, agent_id: String, model: String, system_prompt: String, user_prompt: String, day: int, max_tokens: int, timeout_s: float, heuristic: Callable) -> Dictionary`: Returns {ok, data, source, latency_ms, model, error, raw}. Never fails: falls back to the replay cache (same role/agent, nearest day) and then to the heuristic callable.
- `func live_json(role: String, agent_id: String, model: String, system_prompt: String, user_prompt: String, day: int, max_tokens: int, timeout_s: float) -> Dictionary`: Live-only call for callers that cache per item themselves (resident batches). Never touches the role-level cache; on failure returns ok=false so the caller can fall back.
- `func remember(key: String, day: int, data: Dictionary) -> void`
- `func lookup(key: String, day: int) -> Dictionary`
- `func count_source(source: String, n: int = 1) -> void`
- `static func salvage_array(content: String) -> Dictionary`: Recovers the complete objects of a truncated {"key":[{...},{...},{... reply.
- `static func extract_json(content: String) -> Dictionary`
- `func flush_cache() -> void`: Writes the recorded live responses so offline runs can replay real model output. Outside record mode the session file keeps each key's last 3 days (a pruned copy: session_cache itself stays whole, lookups read it) and is not rewritten when nothing was added since the last flush (the brain flushes at every day end). Record mode writes exactly as before.
- `func avg_latency_ms() -> int`
- `func to_dict() -> Dictionary`
- `func from_dict(d: Dictionary) -> void`

## `scripts/ai/gmi_image_client.gd`

class_name `GmiImageClient` · extends `Node`

Async poster image client for GMI's hy-image-v3.5-preview (slice D). request() returns a cache key at once; the texture arrives later through image_ready, always emitted deferred. Lookup order: memory LRU, user://posters/<key>.webp, the pre-baked set (exact key), the live queue (budgeted, breaker-guarded, never in GRIDFALL_OFFLINE), then the pre-baked pool of the kind and a procedural gradient. While a live image is on the way the request also gets a provisional texture (meta.provisional). Every wait reads `clock` and advances in tick(), so tests run on virtual time. Image processing runs on one background thread (poster_worker.gd). The API key never appears in any printed, stored or saved string.

### Signals

- `image_ready(key: String, tex: Texture2D, meta: Dictionary)`
- `image_failed(key: String, reason: String)`

### Constants

- `QUEUE_URL = "https://console.gmicloud.ai/api/v1/ie/requestqueue/apikey/requests"`
- `MODEL = "hy-image-v3.5-preview"`
- `STYLE_VERSION = "fp1"`
- `CACHE_DIR = "user://posters/"`
- `INDEX_PATH = "user://posters/index.json"`
- `MANIFEST_PATH = "res://assets/posters/manifest.json"`
- `PREBAKED_DIR = "res://assets/posters/"`
- `ART = preload("res://scripts/fp/posters/poster_art.gd")`
- `WORKER = preload("res://scripts/fp/posters/poster_worker.gd")`
- `LRU_SIZE = 32`: Resident textures in the memory cache.
- `DAY_CAP = 6`: D12 budgets.
- `SESSION_CAP = 30`
- `MAX_IN_FLIGHT = 2`
- `BREAKER_FAILS = 3`
- `DISK_CAP = 400`: Kept files in user://posters before the oldest are deleted.
- `DOWNLOAD_LIMIT = 12 * 1024 * 1024`
- `POST_TIMEOUT_S = 120.0`
- `POLL_TIMEOUT_S = 30.0`
- `DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_S = 90.0`
- `SERVES_PER_TICK = 3`: Cache, disk and pre-baked serves handled per tick (each is one small load or a worker start).

### Properties

- `transport: Callable`: (method: String, url: String, headers: PackedStringArray, body: String, to_file: String) -> {"code": int, "body": PackedByteArray}. May be a coroutine. Default: one HTTPRequest per call.
- `allow_live_with_injected_transport: bool`: Test hook: honour the live path under GRIDFALL_OFFLINE=1, but only while `transport` is not the default HTTPRequest transport (an injected fake). The env check stays for the default transport.
- `clock: Callable`: Virtual clock in milliseconds; default Time.get_ticks_msec. Every wait below reads it.
- `player_pos: Callable`: () -> Vector3: the player's feet, which orders the live queue (ctx.player_position).
- `backoff_s: Array`: first and maximum 429 back-off
- `last_error: String`: The last failure, at most 140 characters of the server's body, scrubbed of the key.
- `transport_calls: int`: Transport calls made (tests), and real HTTPRequests the default transport started.
- `peak_in_flight: int`: Highest number of live jobs in flight at once (tests).

### Functions

- `func setup(client: GmiClient, day_fn: Callable) -> void`: client supplies api_key and live_enabled (read only); day_fn returns the current game day (sim.day), which drives the per-day cap and the breaker reset.
- `func close() -> void`: Stops every job (pending results are dropped) and joins the processing thread.
- `static func key_for(prompt: String, size: String) -> String`: Cache key of a prompt: sha256(MODEL|size|STYLE_VERSION|normalized prompt), 32 hex characters. Normalized: trimmed, lower case, runs of whitespace collapsed to one space.
- `func request(kind: String, prompt: String, size: String = "1536x640", priority: int = 0, pos: Vector3 = Vector3.INF) ->`: Returns the cache key immediately. The texture arrives through image_ready, which (like image_failed) is ALWAYS emitted with call_deferred, never inside request(). pos (world) orders the live queue by distance to the player; Vector3.INF means "no position". An empty prompt never goes live (a key restored from a save whose prompt is unknown).
- `func request_key(key: String, kind: String, size: String) -> String`: Like request(), for a key whose prompt is unknown: cache, disk, pre-baked or fallback, never live.
- `func get_cached(key: String) -> Texture2D`: Memory LRU or the user:// file (decoded on this thread), else null.
- `func budget_left_today() -> int`: Live images still allowed today (also bounded by the session cap and what is queued).
- `func in_flight() -> int`: Live jobs submitted and not finished.
- `func queued() -> int`: Live jobs waiting for a submit slot.
- `func breaker_open() -> bool`: True while the failure breaker blocks the live path.
- `func fallback_texture(kind: String, key: String, meta: Dictionary = {}) -> Texture2D`: A pre-baked or procedural texture for kind, picked deterministically by key (never live, never null). meta gets "source" and, for a pre-baked pick, "file".
- `func pool_files(kind: String) -> Array`: The pre-baked files that serve kind (its pool, else its family), sorted.
- `func tick(_dt: float) -> void`: Advances polling, back-off and submit spacing; _process calls tick(delta), tests call it directly.
- `static func long_edge(kind: String, size: String) -> int`: Long edge in pixels for a processed image: 1024 for wide (billboard, hoarding) art and the Gazette, 512 for portrait ads, walls and notices.

## `scripts/ai/resident_minds.gd`

class_name `ResidentMinds` · extends `Node`

Gives every resident a GMI brain. Once a day residents are planned in batches of ten, each batch on a different fast model. When something breaks, the people near it and the people with the right trade are asked how they react. Every answer is cached per resident so offline runs replay what the real models decided; the heuristic below only covers residents nobody has met yet.

### Signals

- `plans_done(day: int)`
- `reacted(ev: Dictionary, responses: Array)`
- `busy_changed(n: int)`

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `MODELS = [ "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash", "google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite", "MiniMaxAI/MiniMax...`
- `BATCH = 10`
- `MAX_REACTORS = 10`
- `EFFECTS = { "fire": "a building is burning and the fire can spread to its neighbours", "blackout"...`
- `PLAN_SYSTEM = """`
- `REACT_SYSTEM = """`

### Functions

- `func setup(p_sim: CitySim, p_people: Residents, p_client: GmiClient, p_brain: Node) -> void`
- `func pending() -> int`
- `func plan_day(day: int) -> void`
- `func spreading() -> bool`: True while spread plan batches or reactions are still waiting for their frame (sliced mode).
- `func finish_spread() -> void`: Runs every waiting spread item now (a save, skip or mode switch needs the whole day planned).
- `func to_dict() -> Dictionary`
- `func from_dict(d: Dictionary) -> void`
